newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO's Freij quits politics after half century.
newsitem.headline: PLO's Freij quits politics after half century.

text.p: Elias Freij, among the Palestinians' most enduring politicians, has resigned from public life after 51 years of service.
Freij, Bethlehem's perennial mayor and the Palestinian Authority official in charge of tourism, quit both jobs saying he was tired.
"A person needs some rest. A few days ago I became 80," Freij told Reuters on Tuesday.

Freij served Bethlehem in the West Bank in one capacity or another under British, Jordanian, Israeli and Palestinian rule, joining its Chamber of Commerce in 1946 during the British Mandate in Palestine.
He was appointed to the city's municipal council in 1960 and remained on the council when Israel captured the West Bank in the 1967 Middle East war.
He has served as the city's mayor since 1972.
Freij was one of the first Palestinian figures to call for a negotiated settlement with Israel, long before the breakthrough 1993 Israel-PLO peace accord.

"In 1972 I said we must challenge Israel with peace and not war and there will be no solution to the Palestinian-Israeli conflict until we take the road to peace. These things were not accepted at the time," he said.
Freij, a Christian, said he was concerned about the shortage of funds to celebrate the year 2000 in Bethlehem, the birthplace of Jesus.
"I am very worried about the Bethlehem 2000 celebrations. We need around $200 million but who will get it?" he said.
Around three percent of Palestinians in the West Bank are Christian.
